## Polling averages update

All numbers are as of 12:00 PM Eastern on Sept. 18, 2026.

### 2026 U.S. House generic ballot

The Democratic margin in the 2026 U.S. House generic ballot ticked up a point this week, with Democrats now ahead of Republicans by 7 percentage points. Currently, 50.5 percent of likely voters indicate that they plan to vote for a Democrat in November, while 43.2 percent plan to vote for a Republican.

results.content: This is a horizontal bar chart showing how 1,461 U.S. registered voters described President Trump in a Sept. 11–14, 2026, Economist/YouGov poll. The most commonly selected descriptions were “corrupt” (53%) and “dangerous” (51%), followed by “out-of-touch” (47%), “cruel” (46%), and “bold” and “racist” (45% each). Fewer voters described Trump as “strong” (37%), “intelligent” (35%), “effective” (33%), “honest” (23%), “inspiring” (19%), or “steady” (18%). results.content: President Donald Trump’s approval rating found a sort of oasis in the desert, rising after weeks of record lows, according to a new Reuters/Ipsos poll released on Monday, Sept. The poll found that 35% of Americans approved of the president's job performance, up two percentage points from the previous Reuters/Ipsos tracking poll released in early September. Trump’s slight improvement in the newest poll came after three straight weeks of the lowest approval numbers he had seen in Reuters/Ipsos tracking since his return to the White House in 2025.
